VERDICT: REVISE — minor statement and scope corrections; the substantive theorems surviveI find no counterexample to the all-parameter rail-freezing obstruction, the corrected whole-receiver charge formula, or the cross-component non-reuse ledger once the hypotheses are stated with the scope required by the cited receiver identity. The rail construction works for every allowed length, both starting parities, boundary intervals, arbitrary feasible exterior data, and mixed promotion bundles.There are two points that should be corrected before treating the note as a fully rigorous written proof.The sentence claiming that “the two unprescribed sites in each end tile” are blank is not uniformly correct for odd-start rails. The boundary-label argument must be split by parity and by whether the last tile is clipped at column  $w-1$ .The generic whole-receiver identity cited from COMPONENT_RECEIVERS_AND_SQUARE_FREE_BOUND.md is stated there for a single-terminal configuration. Section 3 of the new note says only that  $H$  is a complete endpoint component and that the exterior is feasible. Either add the single-terminal hypothesis there, or replace the appeal to the generic identity with an explicit local closed-receiver lemma for this geometry. The local calculation is valid, so this is a proof-scope defect rather than a counterexample to the formula.With those corrections, the result should be accepted.1. Freezing of every rail endpointLet
$$I_i=\{a_i,\ldots,a_i+2\ell_i-1\},\qquad \ell_i\ge 2,$$
and let the rail endpoints be
$$x_c=(-1,c),\qquad c\in I_i,$$
with matching
$$x_{a_i+2j}\mathrel{\text{--}}x_{a_i+2j+1}.$$
The inherited elbow certificate freezes every chamber endpoint and also its mate. This remains true after adding rails: the rails add occupied neighbors but do not remove any selected support, change any prescribed elbow matching edge, or give a chamber endpoint an exterior matching mate.For the rail itself, the two waves are valid.Left-to-right waveThe first endpoint  $x_{a_i}$  seesthe selected cap  $(-2,a_i)$ , andthe frozen chamber endpoint  $(0,a_i)$ .Those are distinct retained neighbors, so  $x_{a_i}$  is frozen. Its mate  $x_{a_i+1}$  therefore remains occupied in every admissible promotion bundle.Inductively,  $x_{a_i+2j}$  seesthe frozen chamber endpoint  $(0,a_i+2j)$ , and $x_{a_i+2j-1}$ , which is the mate of the preceding frozen rail endpoint.Thus
$$x_{a_i},x_{a_i+2},\ldots,x_{a_i+2\ell_i-2}$$
are frozen.Right-to-left waveStarting from the other cap, the same argument freezes
$$x_{a_i+2\ell_i-1},x_{a_i+2\ell_i-3},\ldots,x_{a_i+1}.$$
The two waves are disjoint and exhaust the rail. They use only the two caps, frozen chamber endpoints, and mates of already frozen rail endpoints. They do not depend on the exterior being blank or on the rail beginning at either parity.Consequently, every rail endpoint is frozen under arbitrary feasible exterior data. The retained-mate closure also handles simultaneous bundles: an exterior promotion cannot remove a chamber or rail endpoint that is protected as the mate of a frozen endpoint. The argument is therefore valid for mixed bundles, not merely for isolated single promotions.The separation condition between intervals is sufficient. A blank column prevents two rails from sharing a physical tile, and the caps remain nonadjacent. No additional cross-rail induction is needed.2. Receiver labels and the parity calculationThe old elbow receiver contributes one unit. Its fixed counts are
$$|H_0|=2w+2h-2,\qquad
|R_{H_0}|=\frac w2+h+1,\qquad
|T\cap R_{H_0}|=h+4.$$
Therefore
$$\rho_{H_0}
=(h+4)+\frac{2w+2h-2}{2}
 -2\left(\frac w2+h+1\right)
=1.$$
The added rails lie in the row band  $\{-2,-1\}$ , while the old receiver lies in row bands containing the chamber and elbow legs. Hence the rail receiver tiles are disjoint from the old receiver tiles.For rail  $i$ , let  $t_i$  be the number of selected sites  $(-2,c)$  with  $c\in I_i$ . Since the rail contains  $2\ell_i$  endpoints,
$$\frac{|R_i|}{2}=\ell_i.$$
The only issue is the number of physical receiver tiles and the forced labels at their boundaries.Odd starting columnIf  $a_i$  is odd, the interval begins on a physical column-pair boundary. Away from the ambient right boundary, the rail occupies  $\ell_i$  complete physical column pairs.Each end tile then contains:two rail endpoints in its lower row,one selected cap in its upper row,one remaining upper site.That remaining upper site is forced blank because it is adjacent to the selected cap, which already sees its rail endpoint. There is no lower “outside” site in such a full end tile.If the last endpoint is  $w-1$ , the final physical tile is  $\{w-1,w\}$ . It contains one rail endpoint and the cap at column  $w-1$ ; the upper outside site is blank by cap feasibility, and the lower outside site  $(-1,w)$  is blank because it is adjacent to the original selected support  $(0,w)$ , which already sees the chamber endpoint  $(0,w-1)$ .Thus the receiver has  $\ell_i$  tiles and contributes
$$\lambda_i
=t_i+\ell_i-2\ell_i
=t_i-\ell_i.$$
Even starting columnIf  $a_i$  is even, the first and last rail endpoints lie in partial physical tiles. The receiver has
$$\ell_i+1$$
tiles:  $\ell_i-1$  full interior tiles and two partial end tiles.Each partial end tile contains:one rail endpoint,one selected cap,one upper outside site,one lower outside site.The upper outside site is blank because it is adjacent to the selected cap. For an interior end, the lower outside site cannot be an endpoint by completeness of  $H$ , and cannot be selected because it sees both a rail endpoint and the underlying chamber endpoint. At the extreme columns, the original side supports  $(0,-1)$  or  $(0,w)$  force the corresponding lower outside site blank.Therefore
$$\lambda_i
=t_i+\ell_i-2(\ell_i+1)
=t_i-\ell_i-2.$$
The exact parity formula is consequently
$$\lambda_i=t_i-\ell_i-2\epsilon_i,$$
where  $\epsilon_i=1$  for even  $a_i$  and  $\epsilon_i=0$  for odd  $a_i$ .The top selected sites form an independent set on a path of  $2\ell_i$  positions: adjacent top selections would each see their own rail endpoint and the other selected site. Hence
$$t_i\le \ell_i.$$
Writing
$$L=\sum_i(\ell_i-t_i)\ge 0,
\qquad
E=\sum_i\epsilon_i\ge 0,$$
gives
$$\rho_H
=1+\sum_i\lambda_i
=1-L-2E
\le 1.$$
Thus
$$\rho_H>0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
L=0\ \text{and}\ E=0,$$
that is, every rail must begin at an odd column and must carry a maximum independent set of top selections.The sharp examples are valid. Selecting both caps and the interior offsets
$$2,4,\ldots,2\ell_i-4$$
gives exactly  $\ell_i$  selected top sites and no adjacent selected pair. For an odd-start rail the rail contribution is zero; for an even-start rail it is  $-2$ .There is therefore no parity counterexample and no boundary counterexample to the charge formula.3. The scope issue in the receiver identityThe numerical receiver calculation is correct, including arbitrary feasible exterior data, because the local labels are forced:non-end rail top sites are exactly the counted sites  $(-2,c)$ ;partial-tile upper outside sites are blank by cap feasibility;partial-tile lower outside sites are blank by completeness and feasibility, or by the original side supports at columns  $-1$  and  $w$ ;the old elbow receiver labels remain fixed by its retained supports and completeness;the displayed matching is closed on  $H$ .However, the sentence“Its actual matching is closed, so saturated-tile transfers cancel inside the whole receiver”is not justified merely by closedness under the generic dependency as written. The dependency’s closed-receiver ledger is stated for a single-terminal configuration. Section 3 of the new note does not explicitly state that ambient hypothesis.The minimal rigorous repairs are either:Repair A: add the hypothesisReplace the opening of Section 3 by:Assume now that the ambient feasible pair is a single-terminal representative and that  $H$  is its complete endpoint component with the displayed matching.Then the cited whole-receiver identity applies directly.Repair B: retain arbitrary feasible exterior, but add a local lemmaState explicitly that, for this prescribed geometry, every receiver tile has the displayed labels, every endpoint in the receiver belongs to  $H$ , and every saturated receiver tile has its matching mate within the same receiver. Then the corrected charge formula follows directly without invoking the generic single-terminal theorem.This is a missing scope justification, not a mathematical failure of the rail formula.4. Cross-component non-reuse and the ledgerSection 4 explicitly assumes a terminal configuration whose other components have nonpositive whole charge. Under that stated hypothesis, the ledger is correct.For each elbow  $i$ , choose its capped-corner donor  $Q_i$ . The local donor lemma gives
$$d_{Q_i}=2-|T\cap Q_i|\ge 1.$$
The unique-owner lemma makes the  $Q_i$  distinct for different endpoint components. Let  $Z\ge0$  be minus the sum of the charges of the other components. Since
$$\rho_i=1-L_i-2E_i,$$
the whole-component identity gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\Delta
&=D_{\mathrm{all}}-\sum_H\rho_H\\
&=\sum_{\text{unchosen no-}P\ Q}d_Q
 +\sum_i(d_{Q_i}-1)
 +\sum_iL_i
 +2\sum_iE_i
 +Z.
\end{aligned}$$
Every term is nonnegative:every no-endpoint tile has  $d_Q=2-|T\cap Q|\ge0$ ;each selected elbow donor has  $d_{Q_i}-1\ge0$ ; $L_i,E_i,Z\ge0$ .Thus
$$\Delta\ge0,
\qquad
|T|+|M|\le \frac{mn}{2}.$$
The non-reuse point is also correct. An even-start rail’s  $-2$  contribution is already present in its whole charge through  $2E_i$ . It cannot be charged again as a separate donor loss while the unchanged whole charge is retained. Similarly, the same physical donor cannot be assigned once to the owned-corner certificate and again to an overlapping channel certificate without an additional capacity inequality.The equality characterization in (3) is correct: equality requires every displayed nonnegative term to vanish.5. Concrete obstruction versus the grid targetThe concrete example is valid:
$$w=6,\quad h=4,\quad a=1,\quad \ell=2.$$
The elbow has  $18$  original endpoints and the rail adds  $4$ , so
$$|H|=22,\qquad |M_H|=11.$$
The old receiver has charge  $1$ . The odd-start rail has two receiver tiles, two caps, and contribution zero. Hence the enlarged component still has
$$\rho_H=1.$$
Adding the feasible selection  $(2,2)$  gives the capped donor square
$$Q=\{2,3\}\times\{1,2\}$$
exactly one selected site, so  $d_Q=1$ .The original elbow  $H_0$  is a proper connected frozen subset of the enlarged component, but none of its endpoints can be removed by either single or mixed promotions. This is a genuine counterexample to the proposed general extraction rule that would try to isolate every frozen positive core.It is not a counterexample to the grid inequality. The owned donor pays the unit charge once, the rail contribution is nonpositive, and the exact ledger remains nonnegative. The construction defeats an extraction mechanism while preserving the coefficient-one inequality on the stated receiver class.The scoped Lean file does not alter this assessment. It formalizes the abstract induction and integer ledger arithmetic, but the coordinate boundary labels, component ownership, and global receiver application remain written mathematics, as the note itself acknowledges.
